shots.text: He bought twelve thousand pudding cups for free flights.
You see, in nineteen ninety-nine, David Phillips, a civil engineer in California, spotted a deal.
Healthy Choice gave airline miles for its barcodes. Ten barcodes, five hundred miles.
Mail them in by the end of May, and the miles doubled.
But the cheapest Healthy Choice thing he could find? Pudding cups. About twenty-five cents each.
So he drove to discount store after discount store and bought their pudding.
Twelve thousand one hundred fifty cups. Just over three thousand dollars.
Then came the problem. Every barcode had to be peeled off by hand.
So he made a deal with the Salvation Army. Volunteers peeled the labels, and they kept the pudding.
Donating the pudding even got him a tax write-off of about eight hundred dollars.
The result? More than one point two million miles, and lifetime Gold status with American Airlines.
His story even inspired part of a Hollywood movie. All from cheap pudding.
